'''Gianni Dal Maso''' (born 1954) is an Italian [[mathematician]] who is active in the fields of [[partial differential equation]]s, [[calculus of variations]] and [[applied mathematics]].

==Scientific activity==
Dal Maso studied at [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa|Scuola Normale Superiore]] under the guidance of [[Ennio De Giorgi]] and is professor of mathematics at the [[Scuola Internazionale Superiore di Studi Avanzati|International School for Advanced Studies]] at [[Trieste]], where he also serves as deputy director. Dal Maso has dealt with a number of questions related to partial differential equations and calculus of variations, covering a range of topics going from lower semicontinuity problems for multiple integrals to existence theorem for so called free discontinuity problems,<ref>{{cite journal|title=A variational method in image segmentation: Existence and approximation results|journal=Acta Mathematica|volume=168|pages=89–151|doi=10.1007/BF02392977|year=1992|last1=Maso|first1=G.|last2=Morel|first2=J. M.|last3=Solimini|first3=S.|doi-access=free}}</ref> from the study of asymptotic behaviour of variational problems via so called [[Γ-convergence]] methods<ref>{{cite book|title=An introduction to Γ-convergence|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uB__so7oNWAC|publisher=Birkhauser|accessdate=May 22, 2013|isbn=9780817636791|year=1993}}</ref> to fine properties of solutions to obstacle problems.<ref>{{cite web|title=Caccioppoli prize citation|url=http://umi.dm.unibo.it/caccioppoli/vincitori-en.html#1990|publisher=Italian Mathematical Union|accessdate=May 22, 2013|archive-date=October 11, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171011071928/http://umi.dm.unibo.it/caccioppoli/vincitori-en.html#1990|url-status=dead}}</ref> In the last years he has been considerably involved in the study of problems arising from applied mathematics, developing methods aimed at describing the evolution of fractures in plasticity problems.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Quasistatic crack growth in nonlinear elasticity|journal=Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis|volume=176|issue=2|pages=165–225|doi=10.1007/s00205-004-0351-4|year=2005|last1=Maso|first1=Gianni Dal|last2=Francfort|first2=Gilles A.|last3=Toader|first3=Rodica|bibcode=2005ArRMA.176..165M |s2cid=120920146}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Dal Maso has been awarded the [[Caccioppoli Prize|Caccioppoli prize]] in 1990, the "Medaglia dei XL per la Matematica" by the [[Accademia nazionale delle scienze|Accademia Nazionale delle Scienze]], the Prize of the Minister for the Cultural Heritage for Mathematics and Mechanics by the [[Accademia dei Lincei|Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei]] in 2003 and the Amerio prize by the Istituto Lombardo Accademia di Scienze e Lettere in 2005. He has been invited speaker and the third [[European Congress of Mathematics]] in 2000 and EMS lecturer in 2002.<ref>{{cite web|title=List of EMS lecturers |url=http://www.euro-math-soc.eu/node/1655 |publisher=European Mathematical Society |accessdate=May 22, 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131224110638/http://www.euro-math-soc.eu/node/1655 |archivedate=December 24, 2013 }}</ref> In 2012 he has been awarded an [[European Research Council|ERC]] grant.<ref>{{cite web|title=ERC funded projects|url=http://erc.europa.eu/erc-funded-projects|publisher=European Research Council|accessdate=May 22, 2013}}</ref>
